narrative.summary: Djibouti has no AI-specific law and no published AI strategy. Its AI governance rests on the 2025 Digital Code, whose data protection book limits decisions based solely on automated processing and profiling and creates a data protection commission, and on a December 2025 law creating the National Cybersecurity Authority, which is tasked with assessing AI and other emerging technologies. A first National AI Strategy 2026-2030, confirmed by the digital ministry as a draft under consultation, and an AI regulatory and ethical framework announced by the President are in preparation, but neither has been published.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 019/AN/23/9ème L portant Code Numérique
instruments.english_title: Law No. 19/AN/23/9th L on the Digital Code
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.summary: Djibouti's Digital Code, an eight-book law of 798 articles covering personal data protection, electronic communications, cryptology, e-commerce, consumer law, cybersecurity and cybercrime, and e-government services; it repeals the 2004 ICT sector law. Book One sets GDPR-style data protection rules, creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data, and in Article 65 bars court decisions based on automated assessment of personality and decisions with legal or similarly significant effects based solely on automated processing, including profiling, save where authorised by law, by explicit consent or for a contract with safeguards such as human intervention. Controllers must inform data subjects of automated decision-making and bring existing processing into compliance within one year (two years for public-sector processing).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main legal basis for automated decision-making and profiling safeguards and for the data protection authority that would supervise AI processing of personal data.
instruments.current_status: In force. The law says it is published in the Official Journal upon signature (6 July 2025, special edition n° 04); the eJO page was posted on 18 September 2025, and Law No. 195/AN/25 cites the Code as 'du 18 septembre 2025' - the promulgation date in the law itself is recorded here. Not yet verified from the official text: implementing decrees for each book (Articles 792-797) and the set-up of the data protection commission.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 195/AN/25/9ème L portant création de l'Autorité Nationale de Cybersécurité
instruments.english_title: Law No. 195/AN/25/9th L establishing the National Cybersecurity Authority
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.summary: Creates the National Cybersecurity Authority (ANC), a public administrative body attached to the Presidency under the supervision of the national security directorate, to define and implement national cybersecurity policy, run the national CERT and protect state and vital-infrastructure systems. It defines 'strategic emerging technologies' as explicitly including artificial intelligence, and tasks the ANC with assessing their impact on national cybersecurity, contributing to suitable normative frameworks and to sovereign solutions based on them. It sets up an emerging-technologies and digital-identity unit and allows a research and innovation unit on cybersecurity and strategic emerging technologies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only Djibouti law found that names artificial intelligence; gives the cyber authority a mandate on AI-related security risks and standards.
instruments.current_status: In force: signed 14 December 2025 and published in Official Journal edition n° 23 of 15 December 2025 (article 31: published upon promulgation). The effective date shown is the promulgation date; the law sets no separate commencement date.

leads.title: Stratégie Nationale d'Intelligence Artificielle (SNIA) 2026-2030
leads.issuing_authority: Ministère Délégué chargé de l'Économie Numérique et de l'Innovation
leads.note: Prepared with ESCWA and UNESCO support. The digital ministry's own news page (numerique.gouv.dj, item dated 8 February 2026) confirms a national consultative workshop to examine and enrich the draft strategy, built on four commitments (AI-driven digital transformation, local innovation, digital sovereignty, data protection and citizen trust). 2026-10-18: no official full text or adoption found on the ministry site, in the Official Journal or in Council of Ministers communiqués up to 29 September 2026; the strategy remains a draft.
